thread.title: Apple Stock Falls As iPhone Purchase Intent Hits 5-Year Low | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Falls As iPhone Purchase Intent Hits 5-Year Low | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple stock fell Thursday on new reports of declining iPhone demand. In the U.S., iPhone purchase intent has dropped to a 5-year low as consumers hold on to their existing handsets for longer periods.
X Apple ( AAPL ) sank 1.1% to 174.72 on the stock market today . Since hitting an all-time high of 233.47 on Oct. 3, Apple stock has tumbled more than 25%.
UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri said his firm's latest global smartphone survey provides evidence of lengthening smartphone upgrade cycles, especially in Japan and the U.S. UBS polled 6,900 consumers across five countries for its latest survey.
"For iPhone, purchase intention was down across the board, most significantly in the U.S. and China — the U.S. back to a 5-year low (iPhone 6S levels) and China now at a new low," Arcuri said in a report to clients.

New models usually are 70% to 75% of the mix for both purchase intent and sales, he said. But new models in the latest survey fell to 59% of the mix, Arcuri said.
"Based on the survey, this is largely related to particularly weak iPhone XR demand — a notion matched by ongoing downward XR revisions in the supply chain," he said.
Arcuri reiterated his buy rating on Apple stock, but cut his price target to 210 from 225.
IPhone Sales Estimates Still Too High, Analyst Says Elsewhere, Rosenblatt Securities analyst Jun Zhang maintained his neutral rating on Apple stock, but trimmed his 12-month price target to 165 from 200.
"We have lowered our calendar first-quarter 2019 iPhone shipment estimates twice over the last two months," Zhang said in a report. "We currently forecast Apple will produce about 39 million units and ship about 39 million units for the March quarter. Although we are at the low end of consensus iPhone estimates, we believe the Street will continue to trim down their estimates."
Wall Street's estimates for Apple's fiscal 2020 are too high, he said.
"We believe the lack of iPhone shipment growth, along with tough comps for services revenues, will lead to estimates coming down," he said. "For fiscal 2020, we expect little revenue growth from Apple, mainly due to challenges in the smartphone market."
Zhang also cut his revenue and earnings estimates for fiscal 2019, which started Sept. 30.
